title: Clean zones, contaminated zones and signage
audience: Cleaning and support workers who move between storage rooms, treatment rooms, reprocessing areas and clinical corridors in healthcare settings.
learningOutcomes: Name the items that go in a clean zone, and the items that must stay apart in a contaminated one.
Explain how records, medicines and clean stock are kept out of contaminated areas.
Choose the correct sign category for a given instruction or hazard.

instruction.heading: Two zones in every workplace
instruction.body: A clean zone holds sterile storage, equipment storage, medicines and administration records. A contaminated zone receives items that have been used or soiled, such as reusable instruments waiting for reprocessing, and it includes the receiving area of the reprocessing centre. The two zones must stay apart. Once a clean item has touched something from the contaminated zone it can no longer be trusted, and the organisation has to re-clean or discard it, which costs time and resources.

instruction.heading: Keep the direction of travel one way
instruction.body: Material should move from clean to contaminated, and not back. Reusable instruments that have been used remain in the soiled space until reprocessing is complete, and they are never stored alongside sterile equipment. Single-use items that cannot be reprocessed are dropped into the waste container the facility designates. Where the facility uses separate bins for items soiled with body fluid, use them. Records and medicines are never carried into a contaminated area, and records are never stored with soiled stock.

instruction.heading: Aseptic principles that apply to support staff
instruction.body: Aseptic technique is a clinical procedure, and you do not perform it. The guide does, however, list principles that a support worker needs to understand. The first is the environment: before entering a clean area, check for anything that could let organisms reach a patient, such as an open window, an unclean surface or another activity in progress. The second is no-touch technique. Keep the clean area clean by using gloves, cleaning surfaces, and never letting body fluid enter it. The third is hand hygiene, which must be done before entering a clean area.

instruction.heading: Signs that tell people what to do
instruction.body: Signage identifies clean spaces, soiled spaces and places with a hazard. They can also tell people to act before going into a space, such as putting on protective items, taking off contaminated clothing or cleaning their hands. The guide sets out six sign groups: those that require an action, those that forbid one, those that warn, those that give emergency information, those that signal danger, and those that simply inform. Some signs use only pictures. Before relying on a picture-only sign, make sure the people it is for will understand it. Do not cover, move or remove a sign. Report a missing or damaged one at once.

procedure: Consult the area plan or the supervisor to locate the boundary between clean and soiled space. Do not move a boundary yourself.
Before entering a clean area, wash or rub your hands and put on clean gloves.
Keep records, medicines and clean stock on clean shelves only, never in a contaminated area.
Place used reusable instruments in the contaminated area for transfer, and never return them unwashed to clean storage.
Check that each sign is present, legible and unobstructed, and report any missing or damaged sign with its location.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner who has just cleared a room with soiled curtains is asked to fetch a sterile pack from the clean storage room.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is done with the soiled curtains and the cleaner gloves?
workedExamples.reasoning: Leave the soiled curtains in the contaminated area for their collection route. Change your gloves and wash your hands before entering clean storage, so that you do not carry contamination into it. Ask the nurse in charge to confirm the sterile pack is the correct item.

workedExamples.situation: A sign on the cleaning store door warns of a hazardous area, but the wording is in English only and a worker who speaks another language works the shift.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not for this worker. The sign has to be understood by the people it is meant for. Raise it with the supervisor and ask for a picture-based sign or a translated version. Until the change is made, brief the worker in their language.

equipmentAndPpe: Clean disposable gloves and hand rub or soap and water
Area plan marking clean and soiled spaces
Labelled trolley for the correct route
Spare sign stock or a reporting form for damaged signs

commonErrors.error: Placing used items on a clean shelf because it is nearer.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the designated contaminated area, however far it is.

commonErrors.error: Carrying a cleaning trolley into a clean store.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the route and trolley the facility labels for the job, and keep trolleys for one purpose.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring a sign because the task seems routine.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow every sign on every visit, and report one that is missing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Clean and contaminated zone boundaries are set by the facility. Do not move them, and report any boundary that looks wrong.
Access to waste storage and to locked stores is limited to authorised people. Holding a key does not make a worker authorised; the employer decides.
They have not been checked against an Australian signage standard.
Completing this lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Learner names at least three items for each zone and places them correctly in a scenario.
Learner states how records and medicines are kept out of contaminated areas.
Learner matches each sign category to a correct example.
documentationEvidence: Record of a missing, damaged or unclear sign, with its location, the time and the person told.
summary: Clean and soiled spaces stay separate, and material travels in one direction only, from clean towards soiled.
Support staff apply the environmental and no-touch principles and leave aseptic technique to clinicians.
Signs are kept visible and understood, and a missing sign is reported at once.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item belongs in a clean zone?
options: Sterile storage packs and medicine stock

knowledgeChecks.question: Which category of notice requires a person to act ahead of entry into an area?
Why are used reusable instruments kept in the contaminated zone until they are washed?
options: To keep the trolley tidy and the trolley clean for the next use
To stop them touching clean items and spreading contamination
Because clean items cannot be stored in the same room as the used ones
To make them easy to find for the next client and easy to count
